seeds.title: branches.py exposes helpers the spec does not name
seeds.detail: The module exposes cmd_name, cmd_parse, cmd_list, cmd_preflight, build_parser, JsonArgumentParser, NAME_PARTS, TAILS and the imported datetime and timezone as public names. The spec API names load_format, validate_format, tail, name, split, parse, list_kind, read_rules, evaluate and derive. Prefix the helpers with an underscore, or declare __all__, so importers do not depend on them.

seeds.title: load_format accepts the non-standard JSON values NaN and Infinity
seeds.detail: A config.json whose text is NaN or Infinity, or {"branchFormat": NaN}, gives the default and not a Fail. Python json accepts these tokens. A config file with a UTF-8 BOM gives a Fail. No requirement covers these shapes.

seeds.title: testkit: callPython has no keyword arguments and no TZ control
seeds.detail: callPython in property.mjs passes positional arguments only and fixes the environment. tail and name take keyword parts, and the state tail check needs TZ. The contract tests use a small local consumer helper. Add kwargs and env options to callPython.

seeds.title: tail accepts a non-string part and a non-digit ts
seeds.detail: tail('slice', id=0) returns '0', and tail('state', ts='abc') returns 'state-abc'. parse() in a later slice reads state tails with ^state-(\d{14})$, so a non-digit ts gives a branch that parse does not classify. No S-003 requirement covers it.
